One of the things I've noticed about the alt-right and this new backlash against progressives, is that the people involved within it are smart enough to realize that violence has limited applications for effective social change. When I mean effective change, I'm talking about a fundamental shift in the culture, values, and mores of a nation that benefits the population as a whole. Violence is ultimately counter-productive to this kind of change because it usually responded to with more violence and in most cases it is relatively impossible to completely wipe out a "race" as the options of migration, self-defense, or capitulation become easy choices.

Regardless of the outcome, the groups involved become tainted by the mental and emotional trauma of said violence. No matter how righteous a cause may be or how vicious one's hatred, it still damages everyone involved to such a degree that it takes generations for a population to recover from such tragedies. A great example from Vietnam involved a group of Viet Cong who came across a group of dead US soldiers, and they freaked out believing that these soldiers had been badly burned. They eventually realize that they had stumbled across a group of dead black servicemen and were immediately overcome with emotion.

Sure they hated Americans and thought of them as being just like the French, occupiers and invaders. It didn't stop them from weeping, vomiting, and feeling the nausea of guilt at having taken human lives (even though they had not directly been involved). It wasn't as though they had been indoctrinated with any kind of "progressive" ideas about race, as many of them were from isolated villages and had never seen a black person in their lives, some believing they didn't actually exist. Many of the survivors of that war on both sides walked away with PTSD, can we really expect that it will somehow be "different" this time?

' Sure, the alt-right engages in politically incorrect speech border-lining on racist tirades but that is a whole different kettle of fish to open violence all the way up to murder or ethnic cleansing. In fact, assassinating Trump would make him a martyr and his ideas could potentially be coalesced into some kind of ideological platform. As it stands now, Trump is just a popular candidate. Kill him and his voice would become more powerful than anything leftists could have dreamed of. Suddenly, there would be dozens of "Trumps" rising up all over the place, as those who share his political philosophy but are wary of being killed would commit to strength in numbers.

tl;dr The more Hillary implies that Trump is fair game, the stronger the backlash will be against her and the establishment itself should he actually be killed. A race war would be small potatoes compared to the long-term consequences of such a tragedy.

The righteous anger currently funneled through Trump is almost certainly going to be redirected into outright violence, at least for a short period of time; I'd imagine the main targets would be any group that was perceived as responsible for it and any group that makes the mistake of grave dancing. The biggest danger is that, before this period of violence cools off, a demagogue will appear and capture this poorly-directed anger like lightning in a bottle. The aftermath then becomes entirely dependent on said demagogue's own goals and ambitions - and if he's American Hitler...
